comparator.name: Gezondheidswetenschappen, Beleid & Management Gezondheidszorg
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current programme is a three-year, 180-EC interdisciplinary health-policy and management bachelor organised through nine thematic blocks. Years 1 and 2 cover the Dutch healthcare system, health and illness, healthcare organisations, quality, technology, markets, ageing and welfare. Year 3 combines choice space, Choices and Dilemmas, and a graduation internship with an independently conducted research assignment. No optional route is required for the generic target.
components: Graduation internship and independent research assignment

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Public health, epidemiology and the social-medical foundations of illness
Health behaviour, psychology, ageing and patient experience
Qualitative, quantitative and evaluative healthcare research
Healthcare organisations, management, leadership and communication
Health economics, insurance, markets and affordable care
Health law, ethics, policy and public decision-making
Healthcare technology, innovation and responsible data use
questions: How should healthcare systems balance access, quality, affordability and public responsibility?
How can organisations and technology improve care without neglecting ethics, evidence and patient experience?

selection.assessment: The closest match integrates public health, behaviour, policy, organisations, economics, ethics and research. The programme-interest evidence also supports two coherent and feasible emphases: healthcare economics and market design, and healthcare technology and responsible innovation. They differ materially from the closest curriculum and from one another, so all three alternatives are included.

alternatives.label: Public health, policy & healthcare organisations
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines public health and behaviour with healthcare economics, organisations, leadership, policy and research, matching the comparator’s interdisciplinary centre without claiming specialist professional training.
alternatives.concept: A broad health-policy and management pathway combining population health, behaviour, economics, organisations, public decisions, ethics and applied research.
progression: Foundational health, economics, research and behavioural courses precede advanced health psychology, public economics, organisational leadership and econometrics. Every prerequisite occurs earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned semesters.

alternatives.label: Health economics, markets & evaluation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains health and policy foundations but increases economics, finance, business and data analysis, making affordability and market design the organising emphasis.
alternatives.concept: A health-economics direction focused on insurance, markets, resource allocation, evaluation and evidence-informed healthcare decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this pathway replaces several sociology, leadership and communication courses with macroeconomics, accounting and corporate finance, business foundations and data science, creating a distinct quantitative market-and-evaluation emphasis.
progression: Health, economics and research foundations precede public economics, econometrics and behavioural economics. Advanced health-research courses remain late in the programme. All prerequisites and semester offerings are respected.

alternatives.label: Health technology, data & responsible innovation
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, data science, machine learning, medical imaging, AI ethics and product design form a coherent technology-and-innovation strand grounded in health science and evidence.
alternatives.concept: A health-technology direction combining biomedical and behavioural foundations with data, AI, medical imaging, ethics and innovation.
alternatives.distinctness: This pathway replaces much of the policy, economics and organisation curriculum with programming, databases, machine learning, neural networks, optimisation, imaging and AI ethics, making technology and responsible data use its clear centre.
progression: Programming and mathematical foundations precede data science, machine learning, neural networks and optimisation. Biomedical and research foundations precede advanced health applications. All prerequisites and semester offerings are respected.

notes.text: UCR can approximate the programme’s interdisciplinary academic content but cannot reproduce its integrated Dutch healthcare-system blocks, embedded practice projects, health-law sequence or supervised graduation internship in a healthcare organisation.
